overall.headline: Peak surf and king-tide day on the coast; Iran–US Hormuz tension and Ukraine war spillover continue.
overall.bluf: One ACTION today: stay away from beaches, piers and bluff edges. NWS has a Coastal Flood Warning for the Pacific coast from 6 AM to 4 PM and a High Surf Warning until midnight, with 20–30 ft waves and the year's highest tide near 10:49 AM. Rain moves out by late morning and Thanksgiving looks dry. No FEMA emergency alerts cover Pacifica. Abroad, Iran–US standoff over Hormuz and Russia–Ukraine spillover continue, and stock-market volatility is elevated.

local.note: Surf warning and flood warning today; dry Thursday.

regional.note: King tides flood Bay shoreline; AI-stock volatility.

changes: Updated: NWS (3:53 AM Wednesday) now has the rain moving out by late Wednesday morning and dry weather from afternoon through Thursday. Yesterday's forecast had heavier rain; the Pacifica forecast now shows only a 30% chance overnight.

Updated: San Francisco set a November water-level record Tuesday (8.23 ft). Today's tide is forecast higher. A swimmer went missing at Ocean Beach Monday, and a surfer was found unresponsive off Mussel Rock near Pacifica (Coast Guard via KQED).
New: Thanksgiving fog could affect travel early Thursday (low confidence). NWS says another system arrives Sunday and a stronger one is possible early next week.

New: Colombian police ended a 17-hour supermarket hostage siege in Cartagena; all hostages freed, one gunman killed. China opened an investigation into Politburo member Chen Jining. A US plan for new tariffs on many trading partners is reported.
Update: VIX near 30 and AI stocks fell again; Nvidia shares dropped about 7% (BBC). Brent oil is about $88, down 3.6% on the day.
Update: Iran began rolling power cuts; Iranian media say three ships caught fire after hitting mines in Hormuz (unconfirmed by others).
Dropped as stale: Russian nuclear-satellite report (no new reporting), FBI database item, Hanoi blast, Korean air raid alert, Iraq oilfield takeover, California measles.

coming_up.title: Coastal Flood Warning; high tide near 10:49 AM
coming_up.detail: High Surf Warning runs until midnight tonight. Waves of 20–30 ft are forecast on Pacific beaches.

coming_up.title: Thanksgiving: dry, but fog possible at SFO early
coming_up.detail: Highs in the low 60s. Low-confidence dense fog could delay flights between about 2 AM and 8 AM. High tide Thursday 11:38 AM, 2.2 ft above normal.

coming_up.title: Hazardous beach conditions continue
coming_up.detail: A new westerly swell arrives; small-craft seas of 10 ft or more through Friday.

coming_up.title: Next storm system Sunday; stronger one possible early next week

home_front.summary: Peak surf and flood day: stay off the coast today.

items.title: 20–30 ft surf and coastal flooding today: stay away from the shoreline
items.detail: NWS (3:53 AM Wednesday) forecasts dangerous breaking waves of 20–30 ft, a Coastal Flood Warning for the Pacific coast 6 AM–4 PM with high tide near 10:49 AM, and a High Surf Warning until midnight tonight. Hazardous beach conditions continue through at least Monday. Over the past two days one swimmer went missing at Ocean Beach and a surfer was pulled unresponsive from the water off Mussel Rock. No FEMA emergency alerts cover Pacifica.
items.action: Stay off beaches, piers, jetties and bluff edges and out of the water through Monday; keep children and pets back. Move cars from low spots near the shore, and don't drive through water or around barricades. Skip Beach Blvd around the 10:49 AM high tide.
items.when: Wed 12 AM – midnight; flood 6 AM–4 PM
items.where: Pacifica coast, Beach Blvd, Rockaway, Sharp Park, Linda Mar

home_front.summary: No Pacifica outage found; DreamHost database tools still listed down.

items.title: DreamHost: phpMyAdmin and legacy API still unavailable
items.detail: DreamHost's incident was updated overnight (3:04 AM Pacific Wednesday). It says phpMyAdmin and the legacy API remain unavailable and that the new DreamHost API is scheduled to launch today. Websites are not reported down.
items.action: If a database must be changed, use MySQL Workbench or SSH as DreamHost suggests, and check the status page for the fix.

home_front.summary: No Pacifica closures listed; wave and tide closures possible today.

items.title: Low coastal roads may close at high tide this morning
items.detail: Caltrans lists nothing inside Pacifica; Half Moon Bay paving continues through today. Marin County closed a Hwy 101-to-Hwy 1 ramp and an I-80 lane in Emeryville for tidal flooding Tuesday. I found no Pacifica closure report this morning.
items.action: If waves or water reach the road, expect Beach Blvd and Hwy 1 near Rockaway to close; check QuickMap before leaving and use Hwy 35 or Sharp Park Rd as alternates.

home_front.summary: Air quality good (AQI 35); no local health advisories found.

default.task: Charge phones and power banks, and top off the car's fuel before the weekend storm.
default.why: Another system arrives Sunday and a stronger one may follow early next week.

3d.task: Check you have three days of drinking water, about 1 gallon per person per day.
3d.why: Storms and flooding can briefly disrupt services.

ladder.summary: Surf and tide hazards dominate; see home front.
King tides flood Bay shoreline through Thursday.

items.title: Record king tides flood the Bay shoreline; highest tide of the year today
items.detail: San Francisco's water level hit a November record of 8.23 ft Tuesday; today's peak near 10:49 AM is forecast higher. A Coastal Flood Warning for SF and San Pablo Bay shorelines runs through Thursday 4 PM, and SFO and Oakland airports have flood plans.
items.action: If you travel to SFO, the Embarcadero or the East Bay today, allow extra time and check flight and road status first.

ladder.summary: AI-stock volatility; new tariff plan reported.

items.title: VIX near 30 as AI shares fall again
items.detail: The S&P 500 is near 7,201 (down 0.5% on the day, 6.2% below a month ago) and the VIX is 30.2, up 14%. World stocks were mixed Wednesday after another round of selling in AI-linked shares; BBC says Nvidia fell about 7% on political questions over its CEO's reinstatement. Brent oil is near $88 and gold near $3,539.

items.title: US preparing to unveil new tariffs on many trading partners
items.detail: BBC reports the administration will unveil a plan for new levies hitting many large partners, including China and the EU. Details and timing were not available to me, so price effects are not yet known.

ladder.summary: Russia–Ukraine war spreading; Colombia siege ends.

items.title: Ukraine war spreads: Libya strike kills two Libyan officers; Russian figures show heavy losses
items.detail: Two Libyan naval officers died after Sunday's Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship in Benghazi. Ukraine says drones sank the Merkury; Libyan officials said it was heavily damaged. BBC reports leaked Russian data suggesting almost 500,000 Russian dead.
items.action: No household action; watch for Russian retaliation and Mediterranean shipping disruption.

items.title: Colombian police free all hostages after 17-hour supermarket siege
items.detail: Security forces stormed a Cartagena supermarket and freed about 20 hostages; one gunman was killed (BBC, Guardian).

items.title: Eurostar cancels Paris–London trains after unannounced strike
items.detail: AP says several trains were canceled Wednesday. Check before travelling.

ladder.summary: China purge widens; Solomons drop China pact.

items.title: China investigates Politburo member Chen Jining
items.detail: NPR and the Guardian report the Shanghai party chief is under investigation, the fourth senior Politburo member pushed out in two years.

items.title: Solomon Islands ends security pact with China, signs Australian treaty
items.detail: BBC reports the new prime minister said the country would no longer be a point of regional uncertainty.

items.title: Cambodia hosts largest Chinese military exercise yet
items.detail: The 15-day Golden Dragon-2026 drills began Wednesday, per AP.

ladder.summary: Hormuz standoff; Iran rations power; Gaza strikes continue.

items.title: Iran–US Hormuz standoff continues; Iran reports ships hit mines
items.detail: Iran's Guard says three ships caught fire after hitting mines in Hormuz, per Al Jazeera's Tuesday coverage; I found no independent confirmation. Qatar urged both sides to show restraint. The US naval blockade of Iranian ports continues.
items.action: If it worsens, expect fuel and shipping cost swings; keep the car's tank above half.

items.title: Iran starts rolling power cuts as blockade bites
items.detail: Al Jazeera says Iranian households face about two hours of cuts a day from Sunday, with a gas shortfall of up to 430 million cubic metres a day this winter.

items.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill a Hamas official and family; Saudi coalition strikes Hodeidah
items.detail: Gaza's Interior Ministry says a strike killed a Hamas official, his wife and children; another hit an apartment in the Shati camp. Al Jazeera also reports a Saudi-led coalition strike on Yemen's Hodeidah, with Houthis threatening Saudi ports (single source).
